verses.text: King Solomon loved many foreign women, along with Pharaoh's daughter. There were women from the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites.

They came from the nations the LORD had warned Israel about. He had said, "Do not marry them, and do not let them marry you, because they will surely turn your hearts to follow their gods." But Solomon held on to these women in love.
He had seven hundred wives who were princesses, and three hundred concubines. His wives turned his heart away.
When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart to follow other gods. His heart was not fully true to the LORD his God, as the heart of his father David had been.
Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the hateful idol of the Ammonites.
Solomon did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He did not follow the LORD completely, as his father David had.
Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the hateful idol of Moab, on the hill east of Jerusalem. He built one for Molech, the hateful idol of the Ammonites, too.
He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
The LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
The LORD had commanded him about this very thing, that he must not follow other gods. But Solomon did not obey what the LORD commanded.
So the LORD said to Solomon, "Because you have done this, and have not kept my covenant and my laws that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
But for the sake of your father David, I will not do it while you are alive. I will tear it out of your son's hand.
Even then, I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of my servant David, and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."
The LORD raised up an enemy against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite. He came from the royal family of Edom.
Long before, when David was at war with Edom, Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the dead, and he killed every male in Edom.
Joab and all Israel stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.
But Hadad ran away to Egypt with some Edomite officials who had served his father. Hadad was only a little boy then.
They set out from Midian and came to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh the king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, food, and land.
Pharaoh liked Hadad so much that he gave him a wife: the sister of his own wife, Queen Tahpenes.
Tahpenes' sister gave birth to Hadad's son Genubath. Tahpenes raised him in Pharaoh's palace, and Genubath lived there among Pharaoh's own sons.
While Hadad was in Egypt, he heard that David had died and that Joab the army commander was dead too. So Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go, so I can return to my own country."
Pharaoh asked him, "What do you lack here with me, that you want to go back to your own country?" Hadad answered, "Nothing. But please let me go."
God raised up another enemy against Solomon: Rezon the son of Eliada. He had run away from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
After David defeated Zobah, Rezon gathered men around him and became the leader of a gang of raiders. They went to Damascus, settled there, and ruled in Damascus.
Rezon was Israel's enemy as long as Solomon lived, adding to the trouble Hadad caused. He hated Israel, and he ruled over Syria.
Jeroboam the son of Nebat also rebelled against the king. He was an Ephraimite from Zeredah and one of Solomon's officials. His mother was a widow named Zeruah.
This is how he came to rebel against the king. Solomon was building the Millo and filling in the gap in the wall of the city of his father David.
Jeroboam was a strong and able man. When Solomon saw how hard the young man worked, he put him in charge of all the forced workers from the tribes of Joseph.
At that time, Jeroboam was going out of Jerusalem, and the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open country.
Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
He said to Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself. This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Look, I am going to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand, and I will give you ten tribes.
But Solomon will keep one tribe, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.

I will do this because they have left me and worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in my ways. They have not done what is right in my eyes or kept my laws and rules, as Solomon's father David did.
But I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon's hand. I will let him rule as long as he lives, for the sake of my servant David, whom I chose and who kept my commands and laws.
I will take the kingdom from his son's hand and give ten tribes of it to you.
I will give one tribe to his son, so that my servant David will always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city where I chose to put my name.
I will take you, and you will rule over everything your heart desires. You will be king over Israel.

If you listen to everything I command you, walk in my ways, and do what is right in my eyes by keeping my laws and commands, as my servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a family line that lasts, as I did for David, and I will give Israel to you.
Because of this, I will humble David's descendants, but not forever.'"
So Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam got up and ran away to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt. He stayed in Egypt until Solomon died.
The rest of what Solomon did, all his deeds and his wisdom, are written in the book of the acts of Solomon.
Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
Then Solomon died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam became king after him.
